name: before-you-say-done
description: Run the project's checks and report what they printed, before saying a task is done. Use when finishing any task.

name: make-an-artifact
description: Make an artifact: a folder Slightly Parallel shows on the Artifacts page — a dataset, a document, a page or an app. Use when the operator types #artifact or asks to keep a result as an artifact.

name: task-evidence
description: Attach evidence to a Slightly Parallel task: the proof the operator asked for, plus what the task touched and what it did. Use when the operator types #evidence, or when a task_report answer says evidence is wanted.

name: daily-standup
description: Write the project's standup for yesterday from every chat of that day with a helper agent, and offer to map the program with a second helper. Use when the [slightly-parallel] notice says there is no standup for a day, or when the operator types #standup.

name: log-a-decision
description: Log the decisions made in a piece of work to Slightly Parallel, each with a weight: minor, normal or major. Use when a piece of work is done, when the operator picks between options, when you reverse earlier work, or when the operator types #decision.

name: make-a-scan
description: Write a Slightly Parallel scan: what this chat changed in the project since its last scan, committed or not, then the file entry and the architecture form the scan triggers. Use only when the operator types #scan. Never on your own.

name: write-a-task
description: Write a task onto the Slightly Parallel board from the conversation, the way the operator would type it themselves: #task for later (the agent column), #now for the task this chat starts on (doing), #now-todo and the like for the operator's message filed in a column; a #now task's text is the operator's message, the agent writes the title. Use only when the operator types one of them.

name: keep-the-architecture-page
description: Write the next version of a project's Slightly Parallel architecture page: what the project is, what it does now, what it is made of and what is owed, as claims with their evidence. Use as a step of #architecture when the page is out of date, when the operator types #page, and as the last step of a #scan.

name: map-the-program
description: Map a program for Slightly Parallel: every part of the repository as a row in one table (runtime, entry, surface, api, module, service, store, external, config, build, deploy, test …) and what connects to what. Use when the operator types #map, or when #architecture finds the map out of date. For projects that are programs only.

name: slightly-parallel-help
description: Show the operator the Slightly Parallel commands: what each does and where its result is seen. Use when the operator types #help, or asks what they can type or what a command does.

name: update-the-architecture
description: Bring a project's Slightly Parallel architecture up to date: the architecture form for the last scan, the architecture page and the map of the program, each only when it is out of date. Use when the operator types #architecture (also #page or #map).

name: finish-a-task
description: The operator typed #done: the server has moved the task to done and given it its stretch of the chat. Say what moved, then add your one-line report and any evidence. Use when the [slightly-parallel] #done notice appears.

name: sp-help
description: Show the operator the Slightly Parallel commands: what each does and where its result is seen. Use when the operator types #help, or asks what they can type or what a command does.

name: undo-a-mistake
description: The operator typed #undo: archive the entries a tag made by mistake, only with their numbers and their #undo-yes. Use when the [slightly-parallel] #undo or #undo-yes notice appears.

name: sp-checkup
description: The operator typed #sp, maybe with what worries them: check whether Slightly Parallel works for this chat and folder — recorded messages, MCP, hooks, contract, skills, data, backups, the server's memory and errors — and report what works and what is a concern, without filler. Use when the [slightly-parallel] #sp notice appears, or the operator asks whether Slightly Parallel is working.
